items.title: Shipping Strikes In Hormuz Leave Both Sides With Economic Pain
items.original_title: Shipping Strikes In Hormuz Leave Both Sides With Economic Pain
items.summary: Smoke and fire rise from a commercial cargo vessel following a strike, which US Central Command says it had disabled in the Gulf of Oman after the ship's crew ignored warnings and attempted to run a naval blockade against Iran, at a location given as the Gulf of Oman, October 10, 2026, in this still image taken from a handout video. U.S. Central Command/Handout via REUTERS Oct 31, 2026 (Bloomberg) –As US President Donald Trump threatens renewed attacks against Iran, Tehran’s intermittent strikes on commercial vessels have left the two sides locked in a painful economic standoff. And for the US, the rising cost of shipping oil through the Strait of Hormuz — even though US Central Command says almost all Iranian attacks there fail or are intercepted — has kept fuel prices high, stirring a political backlash at home with the midterm elections fast approaching. But even significant economic pain isn’t likely to change Iran’s ability to keep up “ harassing fire ” in the strait, said Jim Lamson, a visiting research fellow in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London and former CIA analyst focused on Iran and the Middle East.

items.title: Taiwan Says China Harassing Shipping With East Coast Patrol
items.original_title: Taiwan Says China Harassing Shipping With East Coast Patrol
items.summary: A Taiwan Coast Guard patrol vessel moves in Keelung, as China conducts "Justice Mission 2025" military drills around Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan, December 30, 2025. REUTERS/Ann Wang TAIPEI, Nov 1 (Reuters) – China’s Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan’s east coast and trying to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding it had sent its own ships to keep watch. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island’s east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Taiwan’s Coast Guard said China’s “attempts to harass ships at sea through radio communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality.” “Our country holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan, and China has absolutely no jurisdiction over any of Taiwan’s waters,” it added. China on Saturday also sent another Coast Guard ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands, which are strategically located at the top of the South China Sea, Taiwan’s Coast Guard said separately. Taiwan has so far this year “expelled” Chinese Coast Guard vessels from Pratas waters 13 times, it added.
